breaking_changes.BC_description: Dropped support for Node.js versions <18.19.0 and 20.0.0 - 20.4.0, which may cause runtime errors in environments using these unsupported versions.
breaking_changes.Adaptation_method: Upgrade Node.js to version 18.19.0 or later, or 20.5.0 or later, to ensure compatibility.

breaking_changes.BC_description: When the encoding option is set to 'buffer', the output properties (result.stdout, result.stderr, result.all) now return a Uint8Array instead of a Buffer, which may break code expecting Buffer methods or properties.
breaking_changes.Adaptation_method: Replace Buffer-specific methods with Uint8Array equivalents. For example, if using Buffer.toString(), use new TextDecoder().decode(stdout). Example: const { stdout } = await execa('node', ['file.js'], { encoding: 'buffer' }); console.log(new TextDecoder().decode(stdout)); // Decodes Uint8Array to string

breaking_changes.BC_description: Renamed values for the encoding option: null to 'buffer', 'utf-8' to 'utf8', 'UTF8' to 'utf8', 'utf-16le' to 'utf16le', 'ucs2' to 'utf16le', 'ucs-2' to 'utf16le', 'binary' to 'latin1'. Using old values will result in errors.
breaking_changes.Adaptation_method: Update the encoding option values in execa calls. For example: await execa('node', ['file.js'], { encoding: 'buffer' }); // Instead of null

breaking_changes.BC_description: Removed support for passing file paths to subprocess.pipeStdout(), subprocess.pipeStderr(), and subprocess.pipeAll(). Instead, use the stdout or stderr option with a {file: 'path'} object.
breaking_changes.Adaptation_method: Replace pipe methods with stdout or stderr options. Example: await execa('node', ['file.js'], { stdout: { file: 'output.txt' } }); // Instead of .pipeStdout('output.txt')

breaking_changes.BC_description: Removed support for passing writable streams to subprocess.pipeStdout(), subprocess.pipeStderr(), and subprocess.pipeAll(). Instead, use the stdout or stderr option with ['pipe', stream] for streams without file descriptors.
breaking_changes.Adaptation_method: Update to use stdout or stderr options. Example: await execa('node', ['file.js'], { stdout: ['pipe', stream] }); // Instead of .pipeStdout(stream)

breaking_changes.BC_description: Renamed subprocess.pipeStdout(), subprocess.pipeStderr(), and subprocess.pipeAll() to subprocess.pipe(), with a from option to specify 'stdout', 'stderr', or 'all'.
breaking_changes.Adaptation_method: Use subprocess.pipe() with the command and from option. Example: await execa('node', ['file.js']).pipe('node', ['other.js'], { from: 'stderr' }); // Instead of .pipeStderr(execa('node', ['other.js']))

breaking_changes.BC_description: Renamed the signal option to cancelSignal in execa calls.
breaking_changes.Adaptation_method: Change signal to cancelSignal in options. Example: await execa('node', ['file.js'], { cancelSignal: abortController.signal }); // Instead of { signal: abortController.signal }

breaking_changes.BC_description: Renamed error.killed to error.isTerminated in error handling.
breaking_changes.Adaptation_method: Update error checks from error.killed to error.isTerminated. Example: if (error.isTerminated) { /* ... */ } // Instead of if (error.killed)

breaking_changes.BC_description: Removed subprocess.cancel() method; use subprocess.kill() or the cancelSignal option instead.
breaking_changes.Adaptation_method: Replace subprocess.cancel() with subprocess.kill(). Example: subprocess.kill(); // Instead of subprocess.cancel()

breaking_changes.BC_description: Renamed the forceKillAfterTimeout option to forceKillAfterDelay and moved it from subprocess.kill() to execa() options.
breaking_changes.Adaptation_method: Set forceKillAfterDelay in execa options and use subprocess.kill() without it. Example: const subprocess = execa('node', ['file.js'], { forceKillAfterDelay: 1000 }); subprocess.kill('SIGTERM'); // Instead of subprocess.kill('SIGTERM', { forceKillAfterTimeout: 1000 })

breaking_changes.BC_description: Changed the verbose option from boolean to string enum: false to 'none', true to 'short'.
breaking_changes.Adaptation_method: Update verbose option values. Example: await execa('node', ['file.js'], { verbose: 'none' }); // Instead of { verbose: false }

breaking_changes.BC_description: Renamed execPath option to nodePath, and it now only works when the node option is true.
breaking_changes.Adaptation_method: Change execPath to nodePath and ensure node option is true if needed. Example: await execa('node', ['file.js'], { nodePath: './path/to/node', node: true }); // Instead of { execPath: './path/to/node' }

breaking_changes.BC_description: Changed default value of serialization option from 'json' to 'advanced', which may throw errors when sending objects with functions or symbols via subprocess.send().
breaking_changes.Adaptation_method: Avoid sending objects with functions or symbols, or explicitly set serialization to 'json'. Example: subprocess.send({ example: true }); // Remove functions or set { serialization: 'json' }

breaking_changes.BC_description: Manual piping of subprocess.stdout, subprocess.stderr, or subprocess.all must be done immediately after subprocess creation to avoid missing output.
breaking_changes.Adaptation_method: Pipe streams immediately after creating the subprocess. Example: const subprocess = execa('node', ['file.js']); subprocess.stdout.pipe(process.stdout); // Do not delay piping

breaking_changes.BC_description: Signals passed to subprocess.kill() and the killSignal option must be uppercase (e.g., 'SIGTERM' instead of 'sigterm').
breaking_changes.Adaptation_method: Use uppercase signal names. Example: subprocess.kill('SIGTERM'); // Instead of 'sigterm'
